HELICAL-SCAN VIDEO TAPE CASSETTE SYSTEM USING 12s65 mm ( 0'5 in ) MAGNETIC TAPE ON TYPE VHS
SECTION 1. scope 1.1 This standard is applicable to cassettes on two-hand helical-scan video cassette system of 50 Hz-625 magnetic video recording using 12.65 mm ( 0.5 in ) tapt video cassette recorders and defines the basic VHS forma, lines. ONE GENERAL.

1.2 This standard defines the electrical and mechanical characteristics of equipment which wil provide for the interchangeability of recorded cassettes. 8.2 Switching Position and Video Signal overlap - The switching position between the two heads shall lie between five and eight horizontal-scanning lines ahead of the front edge of the vertical synchronizing pulse. The minimum Overlap Of the two video heads shall be three horizontal lines.

13. PAL Chrominance

Signal

Recording

13.1 Recording Method - The chrominance signal is separated from the PAL colour video signal through a band-pass filter with a centre frequency of 4.43 MHz and - 3 dB points at f 600 kHz. The separated chrominance component shall be then down-converted so that its new carrier frequency equals 40 times the horizontal scanning rate plus 1'953 kHz ( 626.952 kHz ), This recording process is illustrated in Fig. 8 ( P 12 ), and explained 3 in 13.2.

IS : 12431

- 1988

13.2 Phase Rotation of the Chrominance Signal - The chrominance signal of channel 2 track only shall be phase-retarded by 90" at every horizontal sync, interval. The channel 1 track remains at 0'. Phase shift should be completed prior to the colour burst. Channel 1 and channel 2 are specified in 8. 13.3 Recording Level - The chrominance signal is recorded with Its record level should be adjusted so that the playback level is corresponding to the saturation record level of this chrominance current. Note - The saturation record leval of the unmodulated chrominance
level no longer increases with increase in record current.
